title: Permutations
oneLinerQuestion: Return all possible permutations of an array of distinct integers.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Permutations problem requires generating all distinct orderings of an array of distinct integers. For an array of size N, there exist exactly N! possible permutations. A naive recursive method constructs permutations by tracking a visited boolean array and building prefixes, incurring extra memory overhead. By applying Backtracking with an in-place swap approach, we partition the array into an already-fixed prefix and an active suffix, generating every permutation directly in-place without auxiliary lookup tables.

- Step 1: Decision Boundary Setup — We define a recursive helper function `backtrack(first)` where the index `first` marks the boundary of the permutation currently being constructed. Elements before `first` are fixed, while elements from `first` to N - 1 represent choices available for the current position.

- Step 2: Base Case & Solution Recording — When `first === nums.length`, all positions in the array have been fixed, forming a complete permutation. We push a deep copy of the current array state (e.g., `[...nums]`) into the global results collection and return to backtrack.

- Step 3: Iterative Swapping & Branching — We loop through available indices using pointer 'i' from `first` to nums.length - 1. To place element `nums[i]` at the current decision slot, we swap `nums[first]` and `nums[i]`. We then advance to the next position by recursively calling `backtrack(first + 1)`.

- Step 4: State Unwinding & Restoration — Once the recursive call returns, we restore the array to its previous arrangement by executing the exact same swap: swap(nums[first], nums[i]). This state restoration guarantees that subsequent iterations of the loop operate on the original array configuration.

- Step 5: Termination & Final Output — After all recursive branches across all indices have resolved, the complete set of N! permutations is populated and returned.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N * N!) because there are N! leaf states in the decision tree, and copying the array at each leaf takes O(N) operations. Space Complexity: O(N) auxiliary call-stack depth for the recursion tree (excluding the space needed to store the N! output permutations).
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION permute(nums):
    res = []
    FUNCTION backtrack(start):
        IF start == LENGTH(nums) THEN APPEND COPY(nums) TO res; RETURN
        FOR i FROM start TO LENGTH(nums) - 1 DO:
            SWAP(nums[start], nums[i])
            backtrack(start + 1)
            SWAP(nums[start], nums[i])
        END FOR
    END FUNCTION
    backtrack(0)
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION
